clue.text: Jacob rashly holding something poisonous

indicators.note: the two words Jacob rashly hold the letters across their join, so the reply sits within them

explanation.surface: A man named Jacob recklessly carries something toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: This hooded snake is venomous, a living example of something poisonous.

clue.text: Take care of the old woman showing sign of severe illness?

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
MA is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A carer looks after an elderly lady who appears gravely ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a link word here; the question mark warns that deep unconsciousness is one sign, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep prolonged unconsciousness can result from grave disease, so it is an example of a symptom.

clue.text: Aim to follow bishop and crook

indicators.note: the aim word comes after the bishop letter, so it follows it in the reply

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A target pursued by a bishop and a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a villain but here it is a verb meaning to curve, as in crooking a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: To crook something is to curve or flex it, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: A new unexciting job collecting silver as a source of security

indicators.note: the dull task gathers the metal inside it

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A fresh, dull job that brings in money gives someone financial security.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place holds a ship secure, and figuratively anything that steadies one is a source of stability.

clue.text: Good queen eating fish as well

indicators.note: the queen's name takes the fish inside, as if consuming it

parts.note: Good Queen Bess is a popular name for Elizabeth I
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A kindly monarch dines on fish too.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Queen Bess is the traditional English nickname for Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in addition or also, so they are synonyms as adverbs.

clue.text: Language that's bent or contorted

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so the letters of bent or are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tongue that is crooked or twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: This Celtic tongue is spoken in Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Tot in poor area, beginning to lose out

indicators.note: the opening of lose is put out of the poor district word

parts.note: a slum is a poor, run-down area

indicators.note: the beginning of the word lose is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small child in a deprived district starts to lose out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but it means a total, as in tot up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a total added up, an informal synonym for an arithmetic total.

clue.text: Reveal record waste?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to waste time is to lose it

explanation.surface: A question about whether a record is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to make known or expose something previously hidden.

clue.text: It's smart catching fish that's drifting

indicators.note: the smarting word catches the fish inside it

parts.note: to smart is to sting, so stinging pain
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Pain from catching a fish that is floating away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering off course is to drift, so the two present participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow outside prison about to get mechanical restriction

indicators.note: the fellow word goes around the outside of the jail word

parts.note: a fellow is a male

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the prison word is read backwards

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A man outside jail is about to be restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the signal to turn the prison word round before the fellow wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A handcuff or shackle is a mechanical device restraining the wrists.

clue.text: Male is having hesitation — he doesn't like spending money

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man hesitates, being reluctant to part with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint hoards money and hates parting with it, which the definition describes.

clue.text: Greatly diminished army officer meets very large girl

parts.note: Col is the shortened form of colonel
OS is the abbreviation for outsize
Sally is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A demoted colonel meets an enormous young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormously and greatly are synonyms describing something on a vast scale.

clue.text: Authorises second performances to get any number in

indicators.note: the number letter is placed inside the performances word

parts.note: actions are deeds or performances
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Someone approves repeat shows to attract more audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to give official approval, so the verb means authorises.

clue.text: Portrayed someone academic and terribly idle

parts.note: prof is short for professor

indicators.note: done badly or out of order, so the letters of idle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar is depicted as dreadfully lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a short descriptive article about someone is to portray or describe them.

clue.text: Soldier and mare crashing into bridge

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the bridge word

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch

indicators.note: the horse crashes and its letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A trooper and his horse crash into a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' is the anagram signal for the horse, whose shuffled letters sit within the bridge word; 'Soldier' is the definition, not the mare's rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier armed with a lance or pike, an example of a fighting man.

clue.text: Duplicate material to demolish?

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
to demolish food is to eat it up

explanation.surface: A question about copying stuff earmarked for knocking down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolish' suggests buildings but here means to wolf down food.
explanation.definitionFit: To duplicate is to do or say again, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Agreement boy should go to HE institution

indicators.note: the boy is placed after the university word, joining it

parts.note: HE is higher education, and a uni is a university
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad ought to attend university.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for higher education, the British term for university-level study.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in harmony or concord is agreement, a synonym in the sense of accord.

clue.text: Wild animal that could be orange

indicators.note: the letters of orange could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A wild creature that might be coloured orange.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild ass of Asia is an untamed beast, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Men in a group try fine art for a change

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters of try fine art

explanation.surface: Men gathered together try fine art as a novelty.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood or society of men, such as a college club, is men in a group.

clue.text: Around home see floor covering

indicators.note: the seeing word goes around the home word

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
in means at home

explanation.surface: Looking about the house, you notice the flooring.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum, shortened, is a material laid on floors, an example of floor covering.

clue.text: Talk with heartless person disobeying rules

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: a cheat breaks the rules

explanation.surface: A conversation with a callous rule-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal conversation, so the noun is a synonym of talk.

clue.text: State of uncertainty with member gaining nothing

indicators.note: the limb word gains the zero letter at its end

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Being in doubt, with an arm or leg gaining nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being stuck in an unresolved, uncertain condition.

clue.text: Fuel in ground, first to come out

indicators.note: the first letter of the ground word is removed

parts.note: soil is the ground

explanation.surface: Fuel in the earth is the first thing extracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is burnt for energy, an example of fuel.

clue.text: Something sticky? Food course is quite nice!

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
a dish is a course of food

explanation.surface: A sticky dessert course turns out to be pretty pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly good is what the word means, so it fits quite nice as an adjective.

clue.text: One hanging around is left in peril

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the peril word

parts.note: danger is peril

explanation.surface: Someone loitering is left in jeopardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dangles hangs loosely, so it is one hanging around.

clue.text: Game one of four card players has left

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; S is South
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A card game where one of the four players has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, so S is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A game such as football is a sport, so the words are synonyms.
